notes: A five-stage video pipeline: (1) HTTP-fetch the mirrored source clip into /app/source.mp4 via a small local mirror server; (2) ffmpeg-trim the source to keep only the trailing 60 frames into /app/clip.mp4; (3) write a pure-CPU frame-analysis script (opencv-headless) /app/detect_frames.py that reports the exact frame where a monocular running subject leaves the ground and the frame where it returns; (4) write /app/extract_commands.py that turns a typed-command session transcript into the ordered verb-phrase commands; (5) emit /app/commands.txt (one command per line) and /app/events.json. The verifier re-executes the two real programs on freshly hidden inputs (three annotated jump clips with clean / never-returns / no-jump scenarios and an unseen transcript) and byte-checks the two emitted files. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (a working end-to-end DAG from download through trim to event detection and serialization), reasoning_depth (invent a position-tracking detection algorithm robust to a coarse baseline and null/ambiguous flight states), adversarial_inputs (hidden clips that never exhibit a takeoff or never exhibit a landing must yield explicit nulls, plus an all-grounded clip = both null, and a malformed/empty transcript), and quantitative_correctness (exact frame indices), with tool_breadth spanning ffmpeg/ffprobe, an HTTP mirror fetch, OpenCV/numpy and CSV-log parsing.
documented_hidden: Nullable takeoff/landing semantics and one-command-per-line ordering are the principal hidden-probe focus.
